title: MAST-Guard: Proactive Failure Detection and Recovery in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Real-Time Taxonomy-Aware Monitoring
description: Problem: While MAST provides a post-hoc taxonomy of MAS failures, no work addresses real-time detection and mitigation of these failures during execution. Systems currently run to completion before failures are identified, wasting compute and degrading reliability in deployment. Proposed Method: We introduce MAST-Guard, a lightweight supervisor agent trained to detect the 14 MAST failure modes in real-time from partial execution traces. Using MAST-Data as training signal, we fine-tune a compact LLM (Llama-3-8B) via supervised learning on (partial-trace, failure-mode, timestep) triplets to predict imminent failures before they propagate. Upon detection, MAST-Guard triggers mode-specific recovery interventions: re-prompting for inter-agent misalignment, sub-task decomposition for verification failures, and architecture restructuring signals for design issues. We additionally train a causal intervention selector that maps detected failure modes to optimal recovery actions using offline reinforcement learning on MAST-Data traces annotated with counterfactual outcomes. Experiments: We evaluate on MAST-Data held-out splits and three live MAS frameworks (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph) across coding (HumanEval), math (MATH-500), and agentic tasks (WebArena). Metrics include failure prevention rate, recovery success rate, task completion improvement, and latency overhead. Ablations isolate detection timing, intervention specificity, and model size effects.

title: MAST-Shield: A Real-Time Failure Detection and Recovery Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
description:

Proposed Method: We build MAST-Shield, an online failure detection and recovery middleware that intercepts inter-agent messages and applies lightweight classifiers—trained on MAST-Data annotations—to predict failure mode probability in real-time. For each of the 3 MAST categories, we design distinct recovery strategies: (i) for system design issues, dynamic role reassignment via a meta-coordinator agent; (ii) for inter-agent misalignment, a structured clarification protocol that forces explicit state synchronization; (iii) for task verification failures, an adversarial checker agent that challenges outputs before propagation. The framework uses a confidence-gated intervention policy: low-confidence predictions allow execution to continue while logging, high-confidence detections trigger recovery.

Experiments: We integrate MAST-Shield into 4 MAS frameworks from MAST-Data (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, MetaGPT) and evaluate on coding, math, and general agent tasks. Metrics include task success rate, failure rate by MAST category, recovery overhead (latency, token cost), and false-intervention rate. We ablate each recovery strategy independently to quantify per-category contribution.
